data.content_ref: inline:Make the school a first-class input: parameterize the grounded extension by an explicit selector that, among a finite family of monotone fixed-point operators, picks the one whose accepted set is the maximal sub-relation satisfying the school's stance (unifier vs. skeptic), computed by a single monotone pass over the operator lattice. Determinism is preserved by committing the school as part of the input; validity of committed roots is then checked per school. The criticizable claim is that the selection rule over schools is itself non-monotone and may be non-polynomial, and that 'maximal sub-relation satisfying a stance' is not well-defined without a canonical ordering over relations — so the proposal may displace the hardness rather than removing it.
